newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Spanish government bonds ended higher on Friday after a roller-coaster ride, but off session peaks as dealers took profits ahead of the weekend.
However, analysts remained positive ahead of the Ecofin meeting on Sunday and Amsterdam summit on Monday and Tuesday.
Traders said a deal on the stability pact had already been priced in by debt markets. "For the market the deal is already there," said an economist at All Trading in Madrid.
The long future, after a record high at 117.16, closed below the psycological level of 117. "That's due to normal profit taking, but the market remains very positive," said a dealer.
"On Monday I would expect the market to climb, or at least not to fall," said Ramon Arechederra at ABN Amro in Madrid.
Despite benign May CPI data -- up 1.5 percent year-on-year versus 1.7 percent in April, market consensus ruled out a rate cut at the next official Bank of Spain repo on Monday.
A Reuter poll conducted after Friday's release of CPI showed a wide majority in favour of the central bank holding its key money market rate at 5.25 percent.
